items.problem: Startup crash in Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll caused by invalid `{StaticResource}` theme-brush references in Styles.xaml.
items.evidence: build-events.jsonl L959 ('The crash is in Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll at startup. Let me check the Styles.xaml for invalid {StaticResource} references that should be {ThemeResource}') through L1012 (rebuild after fixing Styles.xaml).
items.covered_clearly_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md 'Resource references: DynamicResource -> ThemeResource' (line ~779), which explicitly says to migrate system-brush/style references to {ThemeResource}.
items.why_no_skill_change: The skill already prominently documents the StaticResource/DynamicResource -> ThemeResource rule and the agent itself recalled and applied it within a couple of turns. A capable re-run resolves this without any skill edit.

items.problem: App crashes when Printing the Photos scenario (Scenario 5), making Disable Preview (Scenario 6) unreachable.
items.evidence: discrepancies.json crash/Photos and unreachable/Disable Preview; migration-score.json Photos note 'Print is dead (0 tokens, noop) and CRASHES the app process'. No .NET exception type was captured anywhere; the migration agent never exercised the print path (no print run in build-events.jsonl).
items.covered_clearly_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md:336 documents the WinUI 3 printing interop (`PrintManagerInterop.GetForWindow(hwnd)` / `ShowPrintUIForWindowAsync(hwnd)`), which PrintHelper.cs applied correctly.
items.why_no_skill_change: Printing interop — the only clearly generalizable printing concern — is already covered and was applied correctly. The crash has no captured root cause and is confined to one scenario's async photo-preview path, so there is no falsifiable, general skill change to make. Treat as scenario-specific; do not edit the skill on speculation.
